title: Spin fluctuation-mediated unconventional superconductivity in ThFeAsN from first-principles
authors: Guang-Yu Guo, Jau-Wen Liu, Mitsuaki Kawamura
abstract: Superconducting (SC) pairing mechanism, origin of high $T_c$ and symmetry of SC order parameter in Fe-based superconductors are among the important unsolved problems in condensed matter and materials physics. We study the SC properties of ThFeAsN, a Fe-based high $T_c$ superconductor, by {\it ab initio} superconducting density functional theory calculations with electron-phonon coupling, screened static and dynamic electron-electron Coulomb repulsion and spin fluctuation (SF) mediated pair-interaction fully taken into account. Our calculations reveal that ThFeAsN is a SF-mediated multiband superconductor with the calculated $T_c$ of 22.4 K and the $d_{xy}$-wave SC order parameter with different signs on different Fermi surface sheets, in consistent with experiments. We also present distinct SC properties such as quasiparticle density of states and ultrasonic attenuation coefficient which can be immediately verified by experiments.
summary: This theoretical study investigates superconductivity in ThFeAsN by calculating superconducting properties using advanced first-principles methods. The authors determined that spin fluctuation interactions are the dominant pairing mechanism, leading to an unconventional $d_{xy}$-wave order parameter and a calculated critical temperature consistent with experiments.
main_problem: Understanding the superconducting (SC) pairing mechanism, the origin of high critical temperature ($T_c$), and the symmetry of the SC order parameter in Fe-based superconductors.
main_result: The calculations reveal that ThFeAsN is an unconventional superconductor with a $d_{xy}$-wave order parameter, driven primarily by spin fluctuation (SF) mediated interactions rather than electron-phonon coupling.
method: Ab initio superconducting density functional theory (SCDFT) was employed to calculate pairing interactions and the resulting SC gap structure across multiple Fermi surface sheets.
model_or_system: The study focuses on $	ext{ThFeAsN}$, an Fe-based high $T_c$ superconductor, analyzing its electronic structure using DFT methods incorporating electron-phonon coupling (EPC), screened Coulomb repulsion ($\mu_{ee}$), and spin fluctuation interactions ($\mu_{SF}$).
key_observables: Calculated critical temperature ($T_c = 22.4 	ext{ K}$), $d_{xy}$-wave SC order parameter symmetry, quasiparticle density of states (QPDOS), and ultrasonic attenuation coefficient.
important_parameters: $T_c$ comparison with experiment ($\sim 29 	ext{ K}$); relative strengths of pairing interactions ($\mu_{SF}^{nk} > \mu_{ee}^{nk} > \lambda_{nk}$).
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on solving the SC gap equation while treating EPC, Coulomb repulsion, and SF interaction effects separately to determine the dominant pairing mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, momentum-dependent SC gap ($\Delta_{\mathbf{k}}$) across five Fermi surface sheets showing $d_{xy}$-wave character, and comparisons of calculated $	ext{QPDOS}$ and ultrasonic attenuation coefficients.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares different pairing mechanisms (EPC only vs. EPC + e-e repulsion vs. SF interaction) to determine the dominant attractive force, leading to the final conclusion that SF mediation dictates the unconventional $d_{xy}$-wave superconductivity.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the methodology of using first-principles calculations to map out competing many-body interactions ($	ext{EPC}$ vs. $	ext{SF}$) to determine the ground state pairing symmetry is highly relevant to understanding complex quantum phases in strongly correlated systems.
